longTitle.officialTitle: To authorize appropriations for fiscal year 2017 for military activities of the Department of Defense, for military construction, and for defense activities of the Department of Energy, to prescribe military personnel strengths for such fiscal year, and for other purposes.

main.enactingFormula: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This Act may be cited as the “National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017”.

section.heading: ORGANIZATION OF ACT INTO DIVISIONS; TABLE OF CONTENTS.

subsection.heading: Divisions.—
subsection.chapeau: This Act is organized into five divisions as follows:

paragraph.content: Division A—Department of Defense Authorizations.
Division B—Military Construction Authorizations.
Division C—Department of Energy National Security Authorizations and Other Authorizations.
Division D—Funding Tables.
Division E—Uniform Code of Military Justice Reform.

subsection.heading: Table of Contents.—

section.heading: CONGRESSIONAL DEFENSE COMMITTEES.
section.content: In this Act, the term “congressional defense committees” has the meaning given that term in section 101(a)(16) of title 10, United States Code.

section.heading: BUDGETARY EFFECTS OF THIS ACT.
section.content: The budgetary effects of this Act, for the purposes of complying with the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010, shall be determined by reference to the latest statement titled “Budgetary Effects of PAYGO Legislation” for this Act, jointly submitted for printing in the Congressional Record by the Chairmen of the House and Senate Budget Committees, provided that such statement has been submitted prior to the vote on passage in the House acting first on the conference report or amendment between the Houses.

section.heading: AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.
section.content: Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2017 for procurement for the Army, the Navy and the Marine Corps, the Air Force, and Defense-wide activities, as specified in the funding table in section 4101.

section.heading: MULTIYEAR PROCUREMENT AUTHORITY FOR AH-64E APACHE HELICOPTERS.

subsection.heading: Authority for Multiyear Procurement.—
subsection.content: Subject to section 2306b of title 10, United States Code, the Secretary of the Army may enter into one or more multiyear contracts, beginning with the fiscal year 2017 program year, for the procurement of AH-64E Apache helicopters.

subsection.heading: Condition for Out-year Contract Payments.—
subsection.content: A contract entered into under subsection (a) shall provide that any obligation of the United States to make a payment under the contract for a fiscal year after fiscal year 2017 is subject to the availability of appropriations for that purpose for such later fiscal year.

section.heading: MULTIYEAR PROCUREMENT AUTHORITY FOR UH-60M AND HH-60M BLACK HAWK HELICOPTERS.

subsection.heading: Authority for Multiyear Procurement.—
subsection.content: Subject to section 2306b of title 10, United States Code, the Secretary of the Army may enter into one or more multiyear contracts, beginning with the fiscal year 2017 program year, for the procurement of UH-60M and HH-60M Black Hawk helicopters.

subsection.heading: Condition for Out-year Contract Payments.—
subsection.content: A contract entered into under subsection (a) shall provide that any obligation of the United States to make a payment under the contract for a fiscal year after fiscal year 2017 is subject to the availability of appropriations for that purpose for such later fiscal year.

section.heading: DISTRIBUTED COMMON GROUND SYSTEM-ARMY INCREMENT 1.

subsection.heading: Training for Operators.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of the Army shall take such actions as may be necessary to improve and tailor training for covered units in the versions of increment 1 that are in use on the date of the enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall rapidly identify and field a capability for fixed and deployable multi-source ground processing systems for covered units.

paragraph.heading: Commercially available capabilities.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out paragraph (1), the Secretary shall procure commercially available off-the-shelf technologies that—

subparagraph.content: meet essential tactical requirements for processing, analyzing, and displaying intelligence information;
can integrate and communicate with covered units at the tactical unit level and at higher unit levels;
are substantially easier for personnel to use than the Distributed Common Ground System-Army; and
require less training than the Distributed Common Ground System-Army.

subsection.heading: Limitation on the Award of Contract.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may not enter into a contract for the design, development, or procurement of any data architecture, data integration, or “cloud” capability, or any data analysis or data visualization and workflow capability (including warfighting function tools relating to increment 1 of the Distributed Common Ground System-Army) for covered units unless the contract—

paragraph.content: is awarded not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act;

is awarded in accordance with applicable law and regulations providing for the use of competitive procedures or procedures applicable to the procurement of commercial items including parts 12 and 15 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation;
is a fixed-price contract; and

paragraph.chapeau: provides that the technology to be procured under the contract will—

subparagraph.content: begin initial fielding rapidly after the contract award;
achieve initial operating capability not later than nine months after the date on which the contract is awarded; and
achieve full operating capability not later than 18 months after the date on which the contract is awarded.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary of the Army may waive the limitation in subsection (c) if the Secretary submits to the appropriate congressional committees a written statement declaring that such limitation would adversely affect ongoing operational activities.

paragraph.heading: Nondelegation.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary of the Army may not delegate the waiver authority under paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Appropriate congressional committees.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “appropriate congressional committees” means—

subparagraph.content: the congressional defense committees;
the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate; and
the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives.

paragraph.heading: Covered units.—
paragraph.content: The term “covered units” means military units that use increment 1 of the Distributed Common Ground System-Army, including tactical units and operators at the division, brigade, and battalion levels, and tactical units below the battalion level.

section.heading: ASSESSMENT OF CERTAIN CAPABILITIES OF THE DEPARTMENT OF THE ARMY.

subsection.heading: Assessment.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Secretary of the Army and the Chief of Staff of the Army, shall conduct an assessment of the following capabilities with respect to the Department of the Army:

paragraph.content: The capacity of AH-64 Apache-equipped attack reconnaissance battalions to meet future needs.

paragraph.chapeau: Air defense artillery capacity and responsiveness, including—

subparagraph.content: the capacity of short-range air defense artillery to address existing and emerging threats, including threats posed by unmanned aerial systems, cruise missiles, and manned aircraft; and
the potential for commercial off-the-shelf solutions.

paragraph.content: Chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear capabilities and modernization needs.

paragraph.chapeau: Field artillery capabilities, including—

subparagraph.content: modernization needs;
munitions inventory shortfalls; and

changes in doctrine and war plans consistent with the Memorandum of the Secretary of Defense dated June 19, 2008, regarding the Department of Defense policy on cluster munitions and unintended harm to civilians.

paragraph.content: Fuel distribution and water purification capacity and responsiveness.
Watercraft and port-opening capabilities and responsiveness.
Transportation capacity and responsiveness, particularly with respect to the transportation of fuel, water, and cargo.
Military police capacity.
Tactical mobility and tactical wheeled vehicle capacity, including heavy equipment prime movers.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than April 1, 2017, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes—

paragraph.content: the assessment conducted under subsection (a);
recommendations for reducing or eliminating shortfalls in responsiveness and capacity with respect to each of the capabilities described in such subsection; and
an estimate of the costs of implementing such recommendations.

subsection.heading: Form.—
subsection.content: The report under subsection (b) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex.

section.heading: DETERMINATION OF VESSEL DELIVERY DATES.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content:
Chapter 633 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting after section 7300 the following new section:
“SEC. 7301. [10 U.S.C. 7301] Determination of vessel delivery dates
“(a) In General. The delivery of a covered vessel shall be deemed to occur on the date on which—
“(1) the Secretary of the Navy determines that the vessel is assembled and complete; and
“(2) custody of the vessel and all systems contained in the vessel transfers to the Navy.
“(b) Inclusion in Budget and Acquisition Reports. The delivery dates of covered vessels shall be included—
“(1) in the materials submitted to Congress by the Secretary of Defense in support of the budget of the President for each fiscal year (as submitted to Congress under section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code); and
“(2) in any relevant Selected Acquisition Report submitted to Congress under section 2432 of this title.
“(c) Covered Vessel Defined. In this section, the term ‘covered vessel’ means any vessel of the Navy that is under construction on or after the date of the enactment of this section using amounts authorized to be appropriated for the Department of Defense for shipbuilding and conversion, Navy.”
.

paragraph.heading: Clerical amendment.—
paragraph.content:
The table of sections at the beginning of such chapter is amended by inserting after the item relating to section 7300 the following new item:
“7301. Determination of vessel delivery dates.” .

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than January 1, 2017, the Secretary of the Navy shall certify to the congressional defense committees that the delivery dates of the following vessels have been adjusted in accordance with section 7301 of title 10, United States Code, as added by subsection (a):

subparagraph.content: The U.S.S. John F. Kennedy (CVN-79).
The U.S.S. Zumwalt (DDG-1000).
The U.S.S. Michael Monsoor (DDG-1001).
The U.S.S. Lyndon B. Johnson (DDG-1002).
Any other vessel of the Navy that is under construction on the date of the enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: The certification under paragraph (1) shall include—

subparagraph.content: an identification of each vessel for which the delivery date was adjusted; and
the delivery date of each such vessel, as so adjusted.

section.heading: INCREMENTAL FUNDING FOR DETAIL DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF LHA REPLACEMENT SHIP DESIGNATED LHA 8.

subsection.heading: Authority To Use Incremental Funding.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of the Navy may enter into and incrementally fund a contract for detail design and construction of the LHA Replacement ship designated LHA 8 and, subject to subsection (b), funds for payments under the contract may be provided from amounts authorized to be appropriated for the Department of Defense for Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy, for fiscal years 2017 and 2018.

subsection.heading: Condition for Out-year Contract Payments.—
subsection.content: A contract entered into under subsection (a) shall provide that any obligation of the United States to make a payment under the contract for any subsequent fiscal year is subject to the availability of appropriations for that purpose for such subsequent fiscal year.

section.heading: LITTORAL COMBAT SHIP.

subsection.heading: Report on Littoral Combat Ship Mission Packages.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary of Defense shall include in the materials submitted in support of the budget of the President (as submitted to Congress under section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code) for each fiscal year through fiscal year 2027 a report on Littoral Combat Ship mission packages.

paragraph.heading: Elements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each report under paragraph (1) shall include, with respect to each Littoral Combat Ship mission package and increment, the following:

subparagraph.chapeau: A description of the status of and plans for development, production, and sustainment, including—

clause.content: projected unit costs compared to originally estimated unit costs for each system that comprises the mission package;
projected development costs, procurement costs, and 20-year sustainment costs compared to original estimates of such costs for each system that comprises the mission package;
demonstrated performance compared to required performance for each system that comprises the mission package and for the mission package as a whole;
problems relating to realized and potential costs, schedule, or performance; and
any development plans, production plans, or sustainment and mitigation plans that may be implemented to address such problems.

subparagraph.chapeau: A description, including dates, of each developmental test, operational test, integrated test, and follow-on test event that is—

clause.content: completed in the fiscal year preceding the fiscal year covered by the report; and
expected to be completed in the fiscal year covered by the report and any of the following five fiscal years.

subparagraph.content: The date on which initial operational capability is expected to be attained and a description of the performance level criteria that must be demonstrated to declare that such capability has been attained.

subparagraph.chapeau: A description of—

clause.content: the systems that attained initial operational capability in the fiscal year preceding the fiscal year covered by the report; and
the performance level demonstrated by such systems compared to the performance level required of such systems.

subparagraph.content: The acquisition inventory objective for each system.

subparagraph.chapeau: An identification of—

clause.content: each location (including the city, State, and country) to which systems were delivered in the fiscal year preceding the fiscal year covered by the report; and
the quantity of systems delivered to each such location.

subparagraph.chapeau: An identification of—

clause.content: each location (including the city, State, and country) to which systems are projected to be delivered in the fiscal year covered by the report and any of the following five fiscal years; and
the quantity of systems projected to be delivered to each such location.

subsection.heading: Certification of Littoral Combat Ship Mission Package Program of Record.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics shall include in the materials submitted in support of the budget of the President (as submitted to Congress under section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code) for fiscal year 2018 the certification described in paragraph (2).

paragraph.heading: Certification.—
paragraph.chapeau: The certification described in this paragraph is a certification with respect to Littoral Combat Ship mission packages that includes, as of the fiscal year covered by the certification, the program of record quantity for—

subparagraph.content: surface warfare mission packages;
anti-submarine warfare mission packages; and
mine countermeasures mission packages.

paragraph.heading: Limitation on deviation from acquisition strategy.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary of Defense may not revise or deviate from revision three of the Littoral Combat Ship acquisition strategy, until the date on which the Secretary submits to the congressional defense committees the certification described in subparagraph (B).

subparagraph.heading: Certification.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The certification described in this subparagraph is a certification that includes—

clause.content: the rationale of the Secretary for revising or deviating from revision three of the Littoral Combat Ship acquisition strategy;
a description of each such revision or deviation; and
the Littoral Combat Ship acquisition strategy that is in effect following the implementation of such revisions or deviations.

paragraph.heading: Limitation on selection of single contractor.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary of Defense may not select only a single prime contractor to construct the Littoral Combat Ship or any successor frigate class ship unless such selection—

subparagraph.chapeau: is conducted using competitive procedures and for the limited purpose of awarding a contract or contracts for—

clause.content: an engineering change proposal for a frigate class ship; or
the construction of a frigate class ship; and

subparagraph.chapeau: occurs only after a frigate design has—

clause.content: reached sufficient maturity and completed a preliminary design review; or
demonstrated an equivalent level of design completeness.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Littoral combat ship mission package.—
paragraph.content: The term “Littoral Combat Ship mission package” means a mission module for a Littoral Combat Ship combined with the crew detachment and support aircraft for such ship.

paragraph.heading: Mission module.—
paragraph.content: The term “mission module” means the mission systems (including vehicles, communications, sensors, and weapons systems) combined with support equipment (including support containers and standard interfaces) and software (including software relating to the computing environment and multiple vehicle communications system of the mission package).

paragraph.heading: Revision three.—
paragraph.content: The term “revision three of the Littoral Combat Ship acquisition strategy” means the third revision of the Littoral Combat Ship acquisition strategy approved by the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics on March 29, 2016.

subsection.heading: Repeal of Quarterly Reporting Requirement.—
subsection.chapeau: Section 126 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (Public Law 112-239; 126 Stat. 1657) is amended—

paragraph.content: by striking subsection (b); and
by striking “(a) Designation Required.—”.

section.heading: LIMITATION ON USE OF SOLE-SOURCE SHIPBUILDING CONTRACTS FOR CERTAIN VESSELS.

subsection.heading: Limitation.—
subsection.content: None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for the Department of Defense for fiscal year 2017, fiscal year 2018, or fiscal year 2019 for joint high speed vessels or expeditionary fast transports may be used to enter into or prepare to enter into a contract on a sole-source basis for the construction of such vessels or transports unless the Secretary of the Navy submits to the congressional defense committees the certification described in subsection (b) and the report described in subsection (c).

subsection.heading: Certification.—
subsection.chapeau: The certification described in this subsection is a certification by the Secretary of the Navy that—

paragraph.content: awarding a contract for the construction of one or more joint high speed vessels or expeditionary fast transports on a sole-source basis is in the national security interests of the United States;
the construction of the vessels or transports will not result in exceeding the requirement for the ship class, as described in the most recent Navy force structure assessment;
the contract will be a fixed-price contract;
the price of the contract will be fair and reasonable, as determined by the service acquisition executive of the Navy; and
the contract will provide for the United States to have Government purpose rights in the data for the ship design.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: The report described in this subsection is a report that includes—

paragraph.content: an explanation of the rationale for awarding a contract for the construction of joint high speed vessels or expeditionary fast transports on a sole-source basis; and

paragraph.chapeau: a description of—

subparagraph.content: actions that may be carried out to ensure that, if additional ships in the class are procured after the award of the contract referred to in paragraph (1), the contracts for the ships shall be awarded using competitive procedures; and
with respect to each such action, an implementation schedule and any associated cost savings, as compared to a contract awarded on a sole-source basis.

section.heading: LIMITATION ON AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS FOR THE ADVANCED ARRESTING GEAR PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: Advanced Arresting Gear for U.S.S. Enterprise.—
subsection.content: None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2017 for the research and development, design, procurement, or advanced procurement of materials for advanced arresting gear for the U.S.S. Enterprise (CVN-80) may be obligated or expended until the Secretary of Defense submits to the congressional defense committees the report described in section 2432 of title 10, United States Code, for the most recently concluded fiscal quarter for the Advanced Arresting Gear Program in accordance with subsection (c)(1).

subsection.heading: Advanced Arresting Gear for U.S.S. John F. Kennedy.—
subsection.chapeau: None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2017 for the research and development, design, procurement, or advanced procurement of materials for advanced arresting gear for the U.S.S. John F. Kennedy (CVN-79) may be obligated or expended unless—

paragraph.content: the decision to install advanced arresting gear on the vessel is determined by the milestone decision authority for the Program; and
the milestone decision authority for the Program submits notification of such determination to the congressional defense committees.

paragraph.heading: Treatment of baseline estimate.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary of Defense shall deem the Baseline Estimate for the Advanced Arresting Gear Program for fiscal year 2009 as the original Baseline Estimate for the Program.

paragraph.heading: Unit cost reports and critical cost growth.—

subparagraph.content: Subject to subparagraph (B), the Secretary shall carry out sections 2433 and 2433a of title 10, United States Code, with respect to the Advanced Arresting Gear Program, as if the Department had submitted a Selected Acquisition Report for the Program that included the Baseline Estimate for the Program for fiscal year 2009 as the original Baseline Estimate, except that the Secretary shall not carry out subparagraph (B) or subparagraph (C) of section 2433a(c)(1) of such title with respect to the Program.

In carrying out the review required by section 2433a of such title, the Secretary shall not approve a contract, enter into a new contract, exercise an option under a contract, or otherwise extend the scope of a contract for advanced arresting gear for the U.S.S. Enterprise (CVN-80), except to the extent determined necessary by the milestone decision authority, on a non-delegable basis, to ensure that the Program can be restructured as intended by the Secretary without unnecessarily wasting resources.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Baseline estimate.—
paragraph.content: The term “Baseline Estimate” has the meaning given the term in section 2433(a)(2) of title 10, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Mileston decision authority.—
paragraph.content: The term “milestone decision authority” has the meaning given the term in section 2366b(g)(3) of title 10, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Original baseline estimate.—
paragraph.content: The term “original Baseline Estimate” has the meaning given the term in section 2435(d)(1) of title 10, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Selected acquisition report.—
paragraph.content: The term “Selected Acquisition Report” means a Selected Acquisition Report submitted to Congress under section 2432 of title 10, United States Code.

section.heading: LIMITATION ON AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS FOR PROCUREMENT OF U.S.S. ENTERPRISE (CVN-80).

subsection.heading: Limitation.—
subsection.content: Of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2017 for advance procurement or procurement for the U.S.S. Enterprise (CVN-80), not more than 25 percent may be obligated or expended until the date on which the Secretary of the Navy and the Chief of Naval Operations jointly submit to the congressional defense committees the report under subsection (b).

subsection.heading: Initial Report on CVN-79 and CVN-80.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than December 1, 2016, the Secretary of the Navy and the Chief of Naval Operations shall jointly submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes a description of actions that may be carried out (including de-scoping requirements, if necessary) to achieve a ship end cost of—

paragraph.content: not more than $12,000,000,000 for the CVN-80; and
not more than $11,000,000,000 for the U.S.S. John F. Kennedy (CVN-79).

subsection.heading: Annual Report on CVN-79 , CVN–80, CVN–81, and Subsequent Carriers.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Together with the budget of the President for each fiscal year through fiscal year 2032 (as submitted to Congress under section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code) the Secretary of the Navy and the Chief of Naval Operations shall submit a report on the efforts of the Navy to achieve the ship end cost targets for the CVN–79, the CVN–80, the CVN–81, and each subsequent Ford-class aircraft carrier.

paragraph.heading: Elements.—
paragraph.chapeau: The report under paragraph (1) shall include, with respect to the procurement of the CVN-79 , the CVN–80, the CVN–81, and each subsequent Ford-class aircraft carrier, the following:

subparagraph.content: A description of the progress made toward achieving the ship end cost targets, including realized cost savings.
A description of low value-added or unnecessary elements of program cost that have been reduced or eliminated.
Cost savings estimates for current and planned initiatives.

subparagraph.chapeau: A schedule that includes—

clause.content: a plan for spending with phasing of key obligations and outlays;
decision points describing when savings may be realized; and
key events that must occur to execute initiatives and achieve savings.

subparagraph.content: Instances of lower Government estimates used in contract negotiations.
A description of risks that may result from achieving the procurement end cost targets.
A description of incentives or rewards provided or planned to be provided to prime contractors for meeting the procurement end cost targets.

subparagraph.chapeau: A comparison of the ship cost baseline to the most recent budget estimate available as of the date of the report, set forth separately for costs related to—

clause.content: development;
procurement; and
operations and sustainment.

subparagraph.chapeau: For each contract that requires the production of a contract performance report, estimates from the contractor and program manager of—

clause.content: the total cost of the ship at completion, taking into account any changes in costs known or anticipated as of the date of the report; and
the schedule for completion of the ship, taking into account any variances to such schedule known or anticipated as of the date of the report.

paragraph.heading: Commencement and termination of reporting.—
paragraph.chapeau: The requirement to submit a report with respect to a Ford-class aircraft carrier under paragraph (1) shall—

subparagraph.content: begin in the year following the first fiscal year for which funds are appropriated for the procurement of the carrier; and
end on the date the carrier reaches its obligation work limiting date.

section.heading: SENSE OF CONGRESS ON AIRCRAFT CARRIER PROCUREMENT SCHEDULES.

subsection.heading: Findings.—
subsection.chapeau: Congress finds the following:

paragraph.content: In the Congressional Budget Office report titled “An Analysis of the Navy’s Fiscal Year 2016 Shipbuilding Plan”, the Office stated as follows: “To prevent the carrier force from declining to 10 ships in the 2040s, 1 short of its inventory goal of 11, the Navy could accelerate purchases after 2018 to 1 every four years, rather than 1 every five years”.
In a report submitted to Congress on March 17, 2015, the Secretary of the Navy indicated the Department of the Navy has a requirement of 11 aircraft carriers.

subsection.heading: Sense of Congress.—
subsection.chapeau: It is the sense of Congress that—

paragraph.content: the plan of the Department of the Navy to schedule the procurement of one aircraft carrier every five years will reduce the overall aircraft carrier inventory to 10 aircraft carriers, a level insufficient to meet peacetime and war plan requirements; and

paragraph.chapeau: to accommodate the required aircraft carrier force structure, the Department of the Navy should—

subparagraph.content: begin to program construction for the next aircraft carrier to be built after the U.S.S. Enterprise (CVN-80) in fiscal year 2022; and
program the required advance procurement activities to accommodate the construction of such carrier.

section.heading: REPORT ON P-8 POSEIDON AIRCRAFT.

subsection.heading: Report Required.—
subsection.content: Not later than October 1, 2017, the Secretary of the Navy shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on potential upgrades to the capabilities of the P-8 Poseidon aircraft.

subsection.heading: Elements.—
subsection.chapeau: The report under subsection (a) shall include, with respect to the P-8 Poseidon aircraft, the following:

paragraph.content: A review of potential upgrades to the sensors onboard the aircraft, including upgrades to intelligence sensors, surveillance sensors, and reconnaissance sensors such as those being fielded on MQ-4 Global Hawk aircraft platforms.
An assessment of the ability of the Navy to use long-range multispectral imaging systems onboard the aircraft that are similar to such systems being used onboard the MQ-4 Global Hawk aircraft.

section.heading: DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF REPLACEMENT DOCK LANDING SHIP DESIGNATED LX(R) OR AMPHIBIOUS TRANSPORT DOCK DESIGNATED LPD-29.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of the Navy may enter into a contract, beginning with the fiscal year 2017 program year, for the design and construction of the replacement dock landing ship designated LX(R) or the amphibious transport dock designated LPD-29 using amounts authorized to be appropriated for the Department of Defense for Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy.

subsection.heading: Use of Incremental Funding.—
subsection.content: With respect to the contract entered into under subsection (a), the Secretary may use incremental funding to make payments under the contract.

subsection.heading: Condition for Out-year Contract Payments.—
subsection.content: The contract entered into under subsection (a) shall provide that any obligation of the United States to make a payment under such contract for any fiscal year after fiscal year 2017 is subject to the availability of appropriations for that purpose for such fiscal year.

subtitle.heading: Air Force Programs
subtitle.editorialNote: [Section 131 was repealed by section 145 of division A of Public Law 115–232.]

section.heading: REPEAL OF REQUIREMENT TO PRESERVE CERTAIN RETIRED C-5 AIRCRAFT.
section.content: Section 141 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (Public Law 112-239; 126 Stat. 1659) is amended by striking subsection (d).

section.heading: REPEAL OF REQUIREMENT TO PRESERVE F-117 AIRCRAFT IN RECALLABLE CONDITION.
section.content: Section 136 of the John Warner National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2007 (Public Law 109-364; 120 Stat. 2114) is amended by striking subsection (b).

section.heading: PROHIBITION ON AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS FOR RETIREMENT OF A-10 AIRCRAFT.

subsection.heading: Prohibition on Availability of Funds for Retirement.—
subsection.content: None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2017 for the Air Force may be obligated or expended to retire, prepare to retire, or place in storage or on backup aircraft inventory status any A-10 aircraft.

subsection.heading: Additional Limitation on Retirement.—
subsection.content: In addition to the prohibition in subsection (a), the Secretary of the Air Force may not retire, prepare to retire, or place in storage or on backup aircraft inventory status any A-10 aircraft until a period of 90 days has elapsed following the date on which the Secretary submits to the congressional defense committees a report that includes the information described in subsection (e)(2)(C).

subsection.heading: Prohibition on Significant Reductions in Manning Levels.—
subsection.content: None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2017 for the Air Force may be obligated or expended to make significant reductions to manning levels with respect to any A-10 aircraft squadrons or divisions.

subsection.heading: Minimum Inventory Requirement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of the Air Force shall ensure the Air Force maintains a minimum of 93 A–10 aircraft designated as primary mission aircraft inventory until October 1, 2026.

paragraph.chapeau: The Director of Operational Test and Evaluation shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes—

subparagraph.content: the results and findings of the initial operational test and evaluation of the F-35 aircraft program; and

a comparison test and evaluation that examines the capabilities of the F-35A and A-10C aircraft in conducting close air support, combat search and rescue, and forward air controller airborne missions.

paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 180 days after the date of the submission of the report under paragraph (1), the Secretary of the Air Force shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes—

subparagraph.content: the views of the Secretary with respect to the results of the initial operational test and evaluation of the F-35 aircraft program as summarized in the report under paragraph (1), including any issues or concerns of the Secretary with respect to such results;
a plan for addressing any deficiencies and carrying out any corrective actions identified in such report; and
short-term and long-term strategies for preserving the capability of the Air Force to conduct close air support, combat search and rescue, and forward air controller airborne missions.

paragraph.content: Subject to paragraph (2), the Secretary of the Air Force may carry out the transition of the A-10 unit at Fort Wayne Air National Guard Base, Indiana, to an F-16 unit as described by the Secretary in the Force Structure Actions map submitted in support of the budget of the President for fiscal year 2017 (as submitted to Congress under section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code).
Subsections (a) through (e) shall apply with respect to any A-10 aircraft affected by the transition described in paragraph (1).

section.heading: LIMITATION ON AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS FOR DESTRUCTION OF A-10 AIRCRAFT IN STORAGE STATUS.

subsection.heading: Limitation.—
subsection.content: None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for the Air Force for fiscal year 2017 or any fiscal year thereafter may be obligated or expended to scrap, destroy, or otherwise dispose of any potential donor A-10 aircraft until the date on which the Secretary of the Air Force submits to the congressional defense committees a report that includes the information described in section 134(e)(2)(C).

subsection.heading: Notification and Certification.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 45 days before taking any action to scrap, destroy, or otherwise dispose of any A-10 aircraft in any storage status in the 309th Aerospace Maintenance and Regeneration Group, the Secretary of the Air Force shall—

paragraph.content: notify the congressional defense committees of the intent of the Secretary to take such action; and

certify that the A-10 aircraft subject to such action does not have serviceable wings or other components that could be used to prevent the permanent removal of any active inventory A-10 aircraft from flyable status.

subsection.heading: Plan to Prevent Removal A-10 Aircraft From Flyable Status.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of the Air Force shall—

paragraph.content: include with the materials submitted to Congress in support of the budget of the Department of Defense for fiscal year 2018 (as submitted with the budget of the President under section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code) a plan to prevent the permanent removal of any active inventory A-10 aircraft from flyable status due to unserviceable wings or any other required component during the period covered by the future years defense plan submitted to Congress under section 221 of title 10, United States Code; and
carry out such plan to prevent the permanent removal of any active inventory A-10 aircraft from flyable status.

subsection.heading: Potential Donor A-10 Aircraft Defined.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “potential donor A-10 aircraft” means any A-10 aircraft in any storage status in the 309th Aerospace Maintenance and Regeneration Group that has serviceable wings or other components that could be used to prevent any active inventory A-10 aircraft from being permanently removed from flyable status due to unserviceable wings or other components.

section.heading: PROHIBITION ON AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS FOR RETIREMENT OF JOINT SURVEILLANCE TARGET ATTACK RADAR SYSTEM AIRCRAFT.

subsection.heading: Prohibition.—
subsection.content: Except as provided by subsection (b) and in addition to the prohibition under section 144 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (Public Law 114-92; 129 Stat. 758), none of the funds authorized to be appropriated or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2018 for the Air Force may be obligated or expended to retire, or prepare to retire, any Joint Surveillance Target Attack Radar System aircraft.

subsection.heading: Exception.—
subsection.content: The prohibition in subsection (a) shall not apply to individual Joint Surveillance Target Attack Radar System aircraft that the Secretary of the Air Force determines, on a case-by-case basis, to be non-operational because of mishaps, other damage, or being uneconomical to repair.

section.heading: ELIMINATION OF ANNUAL REPORT ON AIRCRAFT INVENTORY.
section.chapeau: Section 231a of title 10, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.content: by striking subsection (e); and
by redesignating subsection (f) as subsection (e).

section.heading: STANDARDIZATION OF 5.56MM RIFLE AMMUNITION.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: If, on the date that is 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Army and the Marine Corps are using in combat two different types of enhanced 5.56mm rifle ammunition, the Secretary of Defense shall, on such date, submit to the congressional defense committees a report explaining the reasons that the Army and the Marine Corps are using different types of such ammunition.

subsection.heading: Standardization Requirement.—
subsection.content: Except as provided in subsection (c), not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall ensure that the Army and the Marine Corps are using in combat one standard type of enhanced 5.56mm rifle ammunition.

subsection.heading: Exception.—
subsection.chapeau: Subsection (b) shall not apply in a case in which the Secretary of Defense—

paragraph.content: determines that a state of emergency requires the Army and the Marine Corps to use in combat different types of enhanced 5.56mm rifle ammunition; and
certifies to the congressional defense committees that such a determination has been made.

section.heading: FIRE SUPPRESSANT AND FUEL CONTAINMENT STANDARDS FOR CERTAIN VEHICLES.

paragraph.content: The Secretary of the Army shall issue guidance regarding fire suppressant and fuel containment standards for covered vehicles of the Army.
The Secretary of the Navy shall issue guidance regarding fire suppressant and fuel containment standards for covered vehicles of the Marine Corps.

subsection.heading: Elements.—
subsection.chapeau: The guidance regarding fire suppressant and fuel containment standards issued pursuant to subsection (a) shall—

paragraph.content: meet the survivability requirements applicable to each class of covered vehicles;
include standards for vehicle armor, vehicle fire suppression systems, and fuel containment technologies in covered vehicles; and
balance cost, survivability, and mobility.

subsection.heading: Report to Congress.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of the Navy shall each submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes—

paragraph.content: the policy guidance established pursuant to subsection (a), set forth separately for each class of covered vehicle; and
any other information the Secretaries determine to be appropriate.

subsection.heading: Covered Vehicles.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “covered vehicles” means ground vehicles acquired on or after October 1, 2018, under a major defense acquisition program (as such term is defined in section 2430 of title 10, United States Code), including light tactical vehicles, medium tactical vehicles, heavy tactical vehicles, and ground combat vehicles.

section.heading: LIMITATION ON AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS FOR DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN CLUSTER MUNITIONS.

subsection.heading: Limitation.—
subsection.content: Except as provided in subsection (b), none of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2017 for the Department of Defense may be obligated or expended for the destruction of cluster munitions until the date on which the Secretary of Defense submits the report required by subsection (c).

subsection.heading: Exception for Safety.—
subsection.chapeau: The limitation under subsection (a) shall not apply to the destruction of cluster munitions that the Secretary determines—

paragraph.content: are unserviceable as a result of an inspection, test, field incident, or other significant failure to meet performance or logistics requirements; or
are unsafe or could pose a safety risk if not demilitarized or destroyed.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than March 1, 2017, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes each of the following elements:

subparagraph.content: A description of the policy of the Department of Defense regarding the use of cluster munitions, including an explanation of the process through which commanders may seek waivers to use such munitions.

A 10-year projection of the requirements and inventory levels for all cluster munitions that takes into account future production of cluster munitions, any plans for demilitarization of such munitions, any plans for the recapitalization of such munitions, the age of the munitions, storage and safety considerations, and other factors that will affect the size of the inventory.
A 10-year projection for the cost to achieve the inventory levels projected in subparagraph (B), including the cost for potential demilitarization or disposal of such munitions.

A 10-year projection for the cost to develop and produce new cluster munitions that comply with the Memorandum of the Secretary of Defense dated June 19, 2008, regarding the Department of Defense policy on cluster munitions and unintended harm to civilians that the Secretary determines are necessary to meet the demands of current operational plans.
An assessment, by the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, of the effects of the projected cluster inventory on operational plans.
Any other matters that the Secretary determines should be included in the report.

paragraph.heading: Form of report.—
paragraph.content: The report required by paragraph (1) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex.

subsection.heading: Cluster Munitions Defined.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “cluster munitions” includes systems delivered by aircraft, cruise missiles, artillery, mortars, missiles, tanks, rocket launchers, or naval guns that deploy payloads of explosive submunitions that detonate via target acquisition, impact, or altitude, or that self-destruct.

section.heading: REPORT ON DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE MUNITIONS STRATEGY FOR THE COMBATANT COMMANDS.

subsection.heading: Report Required.—
subsection.content: Not later than April 1, 2017, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the munitions strategy for the combatant commands for the six-year period beginning on January 1, 2017.

subsection.heading: Elements.—
subsection.chapeau: The report required by subsection (a) shall include the following:

paragraph.chapeau: For each year covered by the report, an identification of the munitions requirements of the combatant commands, including—

subparagraph.content: plans, programming, and budgeting for each type of munition; and
the inventory of each type of munition.

paragraph.content: An assessment of any gaps and shortfalls with respect to munitions determined to be essential to the ability of the combatant commands to fulfill mission requirements.
An assessment of how current and planned munitions programs may affect operational concepts and capabilities of the combatant commands.
An identification of limitations in relevant industrial bases and a description of necessary munitions investments.

An assessment of how munitions capability and capacity may be affected by changes consistent with the memorandum of the Secretary of Defense dated June 19, 2008, regarding the policy of the Department of Defense on cluster munitions and unintended harm to civilians.
Any other matters the Secretary determines appropriate.

section.heading: MODIFICATIONS TO REPORTING ON USE OF COMBAT MISSION REQUIREMENTS FUNDS.
section.chapeau: Section 123 of the Ike Skelton National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2011 (Public Law 111-383; 124 Stat. 4158; 10 U.S.C. 167 note) is amended—

paragraph.content: in the section heading, by striking “quarterly” and inserting “annual”;
in the subsection heading of subsection (a), by striking “Quarterly” and inserting “Annual”; and
by striking “quarter” each place it appears and inserting “year”.

section.heading: REPORT ON ALTERNATIVE MANAGEMENT STRUCTURES FOR THE F-35 JOINT STRIKE FIGHTER PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Not later than March 31, 2017, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on potential alternative management structures for the F-35 joint strike fighter program.

subsection.heading: Elements.—
subsection.chapeau: The report under subsection (a) shall include the following:

paragraph.chapeau: An analysis of potential alternative management structures for the F-35 joint strike fighter program, including—

subparagraph.content: continuation of the joint program office for the program;
the establishment of separate program offices for the program in the Department of the Air Force and the Department of the Navy;
the establishment of separate program offices for each variant of the F-35A, F-35B, and F-35C;
division of responsibilities for the program between a joint program office and the military departments; and
such other alternative management structures as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

paragraph.chapeau: An evaluation of the benefits and drawbacks of each alternative management structure analyzed in the report with respect to—

subparagraph.content: cost;
alignment of responsibility and accountability; and
the adequacy of representation from military departments and program partners.

subsection.heading: Form.—
subsection.content: The report under subsection (a) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex.

section.heading: COMPTROLLER GENERAL REVIEW OF F-35 LIGHTNING II AIRCRAFT SUSTAINMENT SUPPORT.

subsection.heading: Review.—
subsection.content: Not later than September 30, 2017, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the sustainment support structure for the F-35 Lightning II aircraft program.

subsection.heading: Elements.—
subsection.chapeau: The review under subsection (a) shall include, with respect to the F-35 Lightning II aircraft program, the following:

paragraph.content: The status of the sustainment support strategy for the program, including goals for personnel training, required infrastructure, and fleet readiness.
Approaches, including performance-based logistics, considered in developing the sustainment support strategy for the program.
Other information regarding sustainment and logistics support for the program that the Comptroller General determines to be of critical importance to the long-term viability of the program.

section.heading: BRIEFING ON ACQUISITION STRATEGY FOR GROUND MOBILITY VEHICLE.

subsection.heading: Briefing Required.—
subsection.content: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics, in consultation with the Secretary of the Army, shall provide a briefing to the congressional defense committees on the acquisition strategy for the Ground Mobility Vehicle for use with the Global Response Force of the 82nd Airborne Division.

subsection.heading: Elements.—
subsection.chapeau: The briefing under subsection (a) shall include an assessment of the following:

paragraph.chapeau: The feasability of acquiring the Ground Mobility Vehicle—

subparagraph.content: as a commercially available off-the-shelf item (as such term is defined in section 104 of title 41, United States Code); or
as a modified version of such an item.

paragraph.content: Whether acquiring the Ground Mobility Vehicle in a manner described in paragraph (1) would satisfy the requirements of the program and reduce the life-cycle cost of the program.
Whether the acquisition strategy for the Ground Mobility Vehicle meets the focus areas specified in the most recent version of the Better Buying Power initiative of the Secretary of Defense.

Whether including an active safety system in the Ground Mobility Vehicle, such as the electronic stability control system used on the joint light tactical vehicle, would reduce the risk of vehicle rollover.

section.heading: STUDY AND REPORT ON OPTIMAL MIX OF AIRCRAFT CAPABILITIES FOR THE ARMED FORCES.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary of Defense shall conduct a study to determine—

subparagraph.content: an optimal mix of short-range fighter-class strike aircraft and long-range strike aircraft for the use of the Armed Forces during the covered period;
an optimal mix of manned aerial platforms and unmanned aerial platforms for the use of the Armed Forces during such period; and

subparagraph.chapeau: an optimal mix of other aircraft and capabilities for the use of the Armed Forces during such period, including—

clause.content: long-range, medium-range, and short-range intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, or strike aircraft, or combination of such aircraft;
aircraft with varying observability characteristics;
land-based and sea-based aircraft;
advanced legacy fourth-generation aircraft platforms of proven design;
next generation air superiority capabilities; and
advanced technology innovations.

paragraph.heading: Considerations.—
paragraph.content: In making the determinations under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall consider defense strategy, critical assumptions, priorities, force size, and cost.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than April 14, 2017, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report that includes the following:

subparagraph.content: The results of the study conducted under subsection (a).
A discussion of the specific assumptions, observations, conclusions, and recommendations of the study.
A description of the modeling and analysis techniques used for the study.
A plan for fielding complementary aircraft and capabilities identified as an optimal mix in the study under subsection (a).
A plan to meet objectives and fulfill the warfighting capability and capacity requirements of the combatant commands using the aircraft and capabilities described in subsection (a).

paragraph.heading: Form.—
paragraph.content: The report under paragraph (1) may be submitted in classified form, but shall include an unclassified executive summary.

paragraph.heading: Nonduplication of effort.—
paragraph.content: If any information required under paragraph (1) has been included in another report or notification previously submitted to any of the appropriate congressional committees by law, the Secretary may provide a list of such reports and notifications at the time of submitting the report required under such paragraph instead of including such information in such report.

paragraph.heading: Definitions.—
paragraph.chapeau: ln this subsection:

subparagraph.content: The term “appropriate congressional committees” means the congressional defense committees, the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate, and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives.
The term “covered period” means the period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and ending on January 1, 2030.

section.heading: AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.
section.content: Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2017 for the use of the Department of Defense for research, development, test, and evaluation, as specified in the funding table in section 4201.
